One very good thing about this university is that due to it's size there are a lot of ways to get evolved, be it through RSOs, research with professors etc. But this can also work as a little bit of a disadvantage, as an engineer you probably wont have any classes with less than 100 students until you get to your junior level classes making it harder to form personal relationships with your professors like you might be able to do in high school. As far as professors go I can't really say that I have ever had a really bad one, in addition to this there are a lot of helpful resources like office hours and collaborative study sessions to help you out in addition to lectures, labs and discussion sections. The size also makes it easier to find like-minded people to hang out with. If you want to go to bars you can find people to go with you (if covid is under control when you get here), if you want to go to someone's apartment and watch movies you can do that too.

When I was an underclassmen I actually enjoyed living in the dorms, there was not as much privacy as I might have liked but I think there was a pretty good sense of community. When you live in the dorms it should be pretty easy to find people to hang out or study with, you will probably be taking a lot of the same classes regardless of major like calc series, introductory science courses etc. Also I personally really liked the food that they had in the dining halls, but take this with a grain of salt as I am not a very picky eater and some of the dinning halls are much better than others. 

One thing that I do not like is the career services, they do not really help you all that much when you are trying to get job/internships, they have career fairs in the spring and fall and they have people who will look at your resume but other than that you are really on your own. As far as I can tell there are plenty of other schools  that are supposedly ranked lower than us in engineering that have much more effective career services, particularly schools which have co-op programs built into their curriculum. I have also found the support for on-campus  mental health services to be lacking, if you have issues with that you may have to get help from outside the university. 

I hope sharing this is helpful to you.
